summary: Leaving the PDF tab or the import screen mid-import unmounted the tab: on return the button was enabled again, a second batch could run beside the first, and the count and failed list never showed
harness_idea: When an async run outlives its component, add a spec that leaves and comes back mid-run with the IPC held

summary: With one PDF, a failure to add it to the group set the error and then opened the Reader anyway, so the error went unseen; before, one file stayed on screen
harness_idea: Compare each branch of a rewritten single-item path with the old code's order of throw and navigate

summary: When every PDF failed, fileInto([]) still asked each chosen group, and a deleted group reported an error of its own
harness_idea: Skip side calls on an empty result set

summary: The English count said Imported 1 PDFs for one file in a batch
harness_idea: Flag an English catalog string with {n} followed by a plural noun that does not use plural()

summary: The file input did not filter with acceptsFile, so a non-PDF picked through All files reached the parser as a failed import instead of the wrong-file message
harness_idea: Run every way in to a handler (picker, drop, paste) through the same accept filter

summary: The wrong-file message left the previous batch's count on screen
The failed list keyed items by file name, which two dropped files can share
harness_idea: React key lint that flags keys built from a user-supplied name alone

summary: The checkbox and the group picker stayed enabled during a run although the run kept the values it started with
harness_idea: When a run captures settings at its start, disable the controls for them while it runs

summary: No test checked that several PDFs go into the chosen group: fileInto([]) passed every spec
No test checked that an unchecked box sends false: manual fixed to true passed every spec
harness_idea: For a boolean passed through, assert both values reach the boundary

summary: No test checked that one PDF that fails shows why: clearing the error passed every spec
The headers seam accepted non-ByteString values that real fetch headers reject, and all test names were ASCII, so dropping encodeURIComponent passed
harness_idea: Make IPC seams apply the real transport's constraints (Headers) and feed non-ASCII names

summary: The mock accepted a PDF body that was not raw bytes, which the backend refuses with pdf.parseFailed
harness_idea: Mock handlers reject the same malformed inputs as the backend

summary: The real import dedupes the same PDF by sha256 and returns the same id; the mock makes a new article each time, so specs that import identical bodies count articles the backend would merge
harness_idea: Note mock-versus-backend dedupe rules beside the mock handler

summary: No test checked that the pref comes back from the library at start; dropping it from SYNCED failed only tsc
Reading the pref with useState instead of useSynced (missing storage events after the screen opened) still passes; re-measured in the main tree after the worktree watch trap (row 30): still survives
harness_idea: A spec that changes the pref in a second window while the screen is open

summary: The first spec counted the import call straight after setInputFiles, before the async arrayBuffer read
harness_idea: Count IPC calls after a visible result, or poll

summary: Dropping onImported after several PDFs (no library refresh) passes every spec; re-measured in the main tree: still survives
The parent committed six test commits whose lint failed (new Headers for its throw alone) because the commit chain checked tail's exit status, not oxlint's
harness_idea: Check each tool's own exit status before committing; never pipe a gate through tail

summary: The parent's leave-and-return spec relied on a 400 ms delay outliving two tab switches and failed under two workers
harness_idea: Hold IPC with a promise the spec releases instead of a delay

summary: The Markdown tab's 自動で翻訳しない, shared with the PDF tab, stayed enabled during a PDF run, so checking it there showed the PDF tab checked and locked while the run went in unchecked and was translated
harness_idea: When a lock covers a shared value, find every control bound to it

summary: Opened again mid-run from another group's list, the locked chip showed that group, while the run filed into the groups it started with
harness_idea: When a run outlives a screen, let the screen read the run's own inputs on remount

summary: A group picker already open when a run started stayed open and went on changing the shown groups; the lock disabled only the chip
harness_idea: A lock that disables an opener also closes what the opener opened

summary: A finished run's count and failed list stay in the module store for the window's lifetime, and messages translated before storing stay in the old language after a language switch
harness_idea: Store message codes, not translated text, in long-lived state

summary: A PDF parse that never returns keeps the PDF tab and the group chip locked until restart; the backend's spawn_blocking has no timeout
No test checked that several PDFs show a group error beside their count: dropping the error for several files passed every spec
Keeping the last batch's count or error when a new run starts passed every spec
Keeping the last batch's count on a refused drop passed every spec (the picker's path was covered)
harness_idea: Cover each way in to a shared handler, not one

summary: Keying the failed list by name alone passed every spec
harness_idea: Feed duplicate user-supplied names to lists keyed by them; the harness fails on React's duplicate-key warning

summary: vite's server.watch.ignored has **/.claude/**, so an e2e server started inside .claude/worktrees keeps serving the code it started with; a reused server there reports mutants as surviving
harness_idea: Start a fresh e2e server per mutant in a worktree, or keep worktrees outside .claude

summary: The parent's mutation script ran E2E_PORT=5391 mise ... through subprocess with shell=True, which on Windows is cmd.exe; the command never ran and the parent read its failure as Killed for seven mutants
harness_idea: A mutation runner must show the test summary line (N passed / N failed) and compare it with an unmutated baseline before it calls a mutant Killed

summary: The parent's round-2 fix hid the picker under the lock but left it open: the chip said aria-expanded all run, and after several PDFs the picker came back by itself and took the focus
harness_idea: When a lock hides a popover, assert it is closed after the lock lifts, not only while it holds

summary: A screen opened again mid-run keeps the run's groups after the run ends instead of returning to the scope it was opened from; the chip shows them
A group deleted mid-run stays in the chosen ids on remount while the chip hides it, so the next import reports groups.notFound; the same was possible before with the scope's group
holdImports cannot be called twice in one test: the second overwrites the release and the first hold never resolves
A group created in the picker whose creation resolves after a run starts is added to the chip mid-run; the run still files into its own groups, and the window is one IPC round trip
The picker spec's title named only the closing, not that it stays closed after the run
A refused file's message or one PDF's failure came back on a later visit to the tab, since the run state now outlives the component
harness_idea: When state moves out of a component, list which parts should outlive it and which should not

summary: The count counted files, not articles: the backend keeps one article per PDF content, so the same file twice said 2 and was filed twice
harness_idea: Check the backend's identity rule (here sha256 per content) before counting results

summary: Groups are filed once after the run, so an app closed mid-run leaves the imported chapters in no group
Files confirmed in a dialog opened before a run that started by drop or paste are dropped without a word
The tooLargeError parameter could be built inside with the module-level t
harness_idea: oxlint bans importing t into .tsx files (the React Compiler keeps output that read it): the parameter stays

summary: The one-caller importPdf helper and its { id } | { error } result could go into the loop
The onFile/onFiles union existed only so four single-file zones need not change
The refusal with done: null was written twice, and the checkbox's disabled was optional though every caller passed it

The parent's hunk-splitting script sent the patch through a text pipe, which on Windows turned LF into CRLF; git apply failed, but the && chain still ran the last git add and commit, putting all of ImportView's changes into one commit that did not typecheck without the uncommitted hook. The parent reset that unpushed commit and split it again
harness_idea: Send patches to git apply as bytes, and stop a commit chain on the first failing step (set -e) rather than chaining with &&

summary: The number example (01, 02 or 1, 10) sorts the same as text, so it did not show that numbers sort as numbers; both guides now say 2 comes before 10
harness_idea: When docs give an example of a rule, check that the example would come out differently without the rule

summary: The book example read as if it described the order, and the checkbox was named only by its label
The English guide's lines said stays and went in with no clear subject
The design note packed the order into ファイル名の数の順 and said 残りは続ける with no object
A [one-language] marker in any commit since origin/master turns off the changed-lines pairing for the whole batch, not only that commit; the parent checked this range's pairs by hand
harness_idea: Scope [one-language] to the commit that carries it

summary: To compare a failing spec with the base commit, the parent put a worktree outside the repo with a junction to node_modules and removed it with git worktree remove --force, which followed the junction and emptied the main checkout's node_modules; npm ci restored it from the lockfile
harness_idea: Never remove a folder holding a junction with a recursive delete; rmdir the junction first, or copy node_modules instead of linking it

summary: The full e2e run failed two mobile-paths specs because mobile-dist had been rebuilt at 19:47 from other code; rebuilding it from HEAD (npm run build:overlay) made them pass
harness_idea: Rebuild the embedded dists before a full e2e run, or have the e2e setup check them against the source
